questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : Increasing the number of independent features always increases the R-squared value of the model.
S2 : Increasing the number of independent features can decrease the adjusted R-squared if the added features do not improve the  odel significantly.
Which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
(c)
• Adding more independent variables never decreases the R-squared because it measures how well the model fits the data, and more features can only improve or keep the fit same. So, S1 is correct.
• The Adjusted R-squared penalizes adding unnecessary variables. If the new features don't
add significant explanatory power, adjusted R-squared can decrease. So, S2 is correct.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : AUC remains constant regardless of model performance.
S2 : AUC-ROC helps compare different models on classification tasks.
S3 : ROC curve cannot be used if classes are balanced.
Which of the following is false?
questions.solution:
(c)
• AUC varies with model performance. As a model improves, AUC generally increases. So, S1 is false.
• AUC-ROC is useful for comparing different models, as it helps evaluate their ability to
distinguish between classes across thresholds. So, S2 is true.
• ROC curves can be used even if classes are balanced. They provide a visual representation of
performance regardless of class distribution. So, S1 is false.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following Statements:
S1 : In linear regression, the output is always a continuous value.
S2 : In logistic regression, the output is always a categorical value.
Which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
(c)
• In linear regression, the output is always a continuous value as it predicts a continuous dependent variable. So, S1 is correct.
• In logistic regression, the output is always a categorical value because logistic regression is used for binary classification, where the model outputs a probability that is mapped to a categorical outcome. So, S2 is correct.

Consider the following Statements:
S1 : In k-nearest neighbors (k-NN), outliers do not significantly affect predictions because they are based on the nearest neighbors.
S2 : In k-nearest neighbors (k-NN), outliers significantly affect predictions, as they distort the majority class or average of the nearest neighbors.
Which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
(a)
• In k-NN, outliers generally have less influence because predictions depend on the nearest neighbors. While the value of k can affect this, outliers are less likely to significantly change the prediction compared to other models. So, S1 is true.

options.text: F1-score is equal to accuracy in all balanced datasets.

F1-score is sensitive to class imbalance.
F1-score is always equal to specificity.

questions.qtext: Which of the following metrics is most sensitive to class imbalance and may give a misleading impression of performance?
questions.solution:
(d)
In imbalanced classification problems, accuracy can be misleading because a model predicting
only the majority class can still achieve high accuracy. F1-score, which balances precision and
recall, provides a better measure of performance by focusing on how well the model detects the
minority class. Mean Squared Error and R-squared are regression metrics and not suitable for
classification tasks.

questions.qtext: Which of the following is/are true for Naive Bayes classifiers?

options.text: It requires the calculation of prior probabilities of classes.
It cannot handle continuous data without discretization or distribution assumptions.
It is robust to irrelevant features due to its independence assumption.
It assumes features are dependent on each other.

questions.solution:
(a, c)
• Prior probabilities are needed for posterior calculation. So, option (a) is correct.
• Naive Bayes can handle continuous data by assuming distributions like Gaussian. So, option (b) is false.
• Independence assumption helps reduce the effect of irrelevant features. So, option (c) is true.
• Naive Bayes assumes features are conditionally independent, not dependent. So, option (d) is false.

options.text: In linear regression, there may be collinearity between the independent variables.
In linear regression, there may be collinearity between the dependent variables.
In logistic regression, there should be little to no collinearity between dependent variables.
In logistic regression, there should be little to no collinearity between independent variables.

questions.solution:
(a, d)
• In linear regression, collinearity can occur between independent variables, leading to multicollinearity and unstable estimates. However, there is no collinearity between dependent variables, as there is only one dependent variable in linear regression.
• In logistic regression, high collinearity between independent variables can lead to unreliable estimates, so it should be avoided. However, collinearity does not apply to dependent variables, as there is only one dependent variable in logistic regression.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are true?

options.text: Ridge Regression prevents overfitting by shrinking coefficients using L2 regularization..
Ridge Regression does perform the feature selection.
Lasso Regression does perform the feature selection.
Lasso Regression prevents overfitting by eliminating irrelevant features through L1 regularization.

questions.solution:
(a, c, d)
• Ridge Regression uses L2 regularization to shrink large coefficients, which helps in preventing overfitting. So, option (a) is correct.
• Ridge Regression uses L2 regularization, which shrinks coefficients but does not reduce them to zero. As a result, it retains all features and does not perform feature selection. So, option(b) is incorrect.
• Lasso Regression uses L1 regularization, which can shrink some coefficients to exactly zero.
This effectively removes those features from the model, so Lasso performs feature selection.
So, option (c) is correct
• Lasso Regression uses L1 regularization, which can shrink some coefficients to exactly zero,
effectively performing feature selection. So, option (d) is correct.
